convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for the CorrectedAverage indicator and depends on external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for all trade execution logic (position open/close, money management, new bar detection, history loading).

derived_values.name: dLevel - breakthrough level in price units
derived_values.used_by: entry and exit signal threshold comparison

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars required before calculation

other_exits: Long position closed when Close[1] < CorrectedAverage[1] - dLevel (sell signal triggers BUY_Close if BuyPosClose is true)
Short position closed when Close[1] > CorrectedAverage[1] + dLevel (buy signal triggers SELL_Close if SellPosClose is true)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM parameter: negative values represent fixed lot size (e.g. -0.1 = 0.1 lots), positive values represent share/fraction of deposit in a deal. Actual logic handled by TradeAlgorithms.mqh.

custom_logic_notes: Breakthrough system: entry requires previous bar (SignalBar+1) to be beyond CorrectedAverage +/- dLevel AND the bar before that (SignalBar) to be on the other side of the threshold, confirming a fresh crossover of the level. The BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose boolean inputs act as gate switches to enable/disable specific trade directions and closes. SignalBar=1 means signals are calculated on the last closed bar (bar index 1) relative to the current bar, with a confirmation check on bar index 0 (one bar older). Recount flag ensures data is re-fetched if CopyBuffer/CopyClose fails. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library handles all actual order placement, position management, new bar detection (CIsNewBar class), and history loading - these must be reverse-engineered or reimplemented for Python conversion.
python_conversion_notes: The CorrectedAverage custom indicator must be ported to Python first or its formula obtained. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library must be fully reverse-engineered to understand position sizing logic (MM negative=fixed lots, positive=deposit fraction), position checking before entry, and order execution details. The breakthrough logic is straightforward: compare Close against CorrectedAverage +/- Level*_Point across two consecutive bars. The new bar guard (CIsNewBar) must be implemented. SignalBar parameter shifts which bars are compared - with SignalBar=1, it checks the most recent closed bar vs the one before it. The min_rates_total calculation ensures enough indicator data exists before trading. GlobalVariableDel_ cleanup on deinit suggests persistent state management in the trading library.
